prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: parking lot collision in Pearland, Texas. Injury: neck and back strain. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1254; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd prefer to keep my name out of the transcript for now, since this is a test document. I can answer the other questions.

Q: Fair enough. Where were you on the day of the collision?
A: I was in a parking lot in Pearland, Texas, near the entrance of a grocery store. I had just pulled into a space and was getting out of my vehicle.

Q: Can you describe how the collision happened?
A: Another vehicle was backing out of a space two rows over. I saw it moving, but I thought it was clear. It struck the rear driver's side of my car while I was standing beside the open door.

Q: Were you hurt at the scene?
A: My neck felt stiff and my lower back ached almost immediately. I didn't think it was serious at first, but by evening the pain had gotten worse.

Q: Did you seek medical treatment?
A: Yes. I went to an urgent care clinic the following morning. They diagnosed a neck strain and a lower back strain, and they told me to rest and take anti-inflammatory medication.

Q: Have you continued treatment since then?
A: I've done physical therapy about twice a week. The therapist works on my neck mobility and my back. I also have a follow-up with my primary care doctor every few weeks.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?
A: Simple things are harder. I struggle to lift grocery bags, and I can't sit through a full work shift without shifting positions constantly. I used to play in a recreational volleyball league, and I've had to stop.

Q: Has anyone helped you with household tasks?
A: My partner has taken over most of the laundry and vacuuming. My neighbor helped carry things up the stairs a few times when my back was especially bad.

Q: Before this collision, did you have any prior problems with your neck or back?
A: I had some occasional stiffness after long days at my desk, but nothing that required a doctor or kept me from working. It was manageable with stretching.

Q: Have you been able to return to your normal work duties?
A: I went back to work after about two weeks, but on modified duty. I'm still not at full capacity, and I take breaks more often than I used to.

Q: Is there anything else about the collision or your injuries you think is important for this record?
A: Only that I'm still doing therapy and I hope to get back to my regular activities. I'd like the record to reflect that I've tried to follow every treatment recommendation I've been given.
